Matt Leinart orchestrated three touchdown passes, including a 53-yard strike to Reggie Bush in the third quarter that broke the game open after Virginia Tech had stayed competitive through the first half. Bryan Randall's consistent ground game kept the Hokies in the contest early, and Virginia Tech's defense forced an interception in the first quarter, but USC's balanced offensive approach and turnover-free performance ultimately proved decisive. The Trojans' fourth-quarter field goal by Ryan Killeen with under a minute remaining sealed a dominant road win for the defending belt holder.

LenDale White was the star for USC, scoring three touchdowns in the first half alone, including an 11-yard rushing TD in the first quarter and a 1-yard score in the second quarter that exemplified the Trojans' control. Colorado State managed only a few bright spots, like Uldis Jaunarajs' 38-yard rush and a 26-yard completion to Johnny Walker, but the Rams' offense was crippled by turnovers and an inability to sustain drives. Matt Leinart orchestrated the USC offense efficiently with key completions to Chris McFoy and Steve Smith, while the defense recorded multiple interceptions of Justin Holland, including a 56-yard return for a touchdown by Matt Grootegoed. The belt stayed in Los Angeles as USC's defense and ball security dominated what became a complete mismatch.

BYU's defense couldn't contain USC's ground game, which totaled 278 yards, and the Cougars' offense sputtered throughout the night, committing four turnovers including three interceptions thrown by John Beck. Despite a brief spark in the third quarter when Todd Watkins hauled in a 69-yard touchdown reception from Beck, USC's offense simply had too much firepower, with Leinart also scoring on a 1-yard rushing touchdown in the fourth quarter.

Lemon break free for an 82-yard touchdown run with just 10 seconds left in the half, giving Stanford a 28-24 advantage. recap.recap: USC's defense suffocated Oklahoma's offense in this Orange Bowl matchup, forcing five turnovers while committing none of their own in a dominant 55-19 victory that saw the Trojans keep the belt. Despite Oklahoma controlling time of possession with over 21 minutes, the Sooners' five giveaways proved catastrophic, preventing them from converting opportunities into sustained drives. USC's balanced offensive attack of 525 total yards, anchored by a strong passing game of 341 yards, proved too much for Oklahoma to contain. The Trojans' defense forced turnovers at crucial moments to stall Oklahoma's momentum, while USC's efficient offense—though converting just 4 of 14 third downs—capitalized on short fields created by the turnover advantage. This defensive masterclass on the national stage underscored why USC maintained the lineal championship.

Reggie Bush added two rushing touchdowns, while Hawai'i managed only a pair of field goals and one touchdown pass to Bryan Maneafaiga in the third quarter. The Trojans' defense also recovered a fumble in the endzone for another score late in the third quarter, sealing a dominant 63-17 victory that left no doubt about who belonged to the belt.

Texas added two more scores in the fourth quarter, including a defensive touchdown when Aaron Lewis recovered a fumble in the end zone, to cruise to a 56-7 victory and retain the belt.

The Buckeyes struck first with a quick touchdown drive capped by Smith's 14-yard scoring pass to Anthony Gonzalez early in the first quarter, then added another touchdown just before halftime on Smith's 29-yard connection with Ginn Jr. to take a 21-7 lead into the break. Texas managed only one touchdown in response, a 2-yard pass from Colt McCoy to Billy Pittman in the second quarter, and the Longhorns' defense couldn't generate enough pressure on Smith, who completed passes at will. Ohio State put the game out of reach in the fourth quarter with Antonio Pittman's 2-yard rushing touchdown, while Texas's offense struggled with only 3 third-down conversions and two turnovers including an interception in the third quarter. The Belt changed hands on the strength of Ohio State's balanced attack and Texas's inability to contain the Buckeye passing game.

Despite Baylor's overall statistical advantage with 335 total yards and 273 rushing yards, the Frogs' opportunistic defense and Boykin's ability to convert in key moments proved decisive in the closing stages, with TCU scoring late to secure the belt.

But Arkansas, despite being outgained significantly and converting just 7 of 16 third downs, stayed resilient and got a crucial final drive capped by Austin Allen's 16-yard touchdown pass to Keon Hatcher with 1:03 left, followed by a two-point conversion to Allen to secure the stunning upset. The Razorbacks' time-of-possession advantage (33:07 to 26:53) and turnover-free performance proved decisive in a back-and-forth affair that featured eight total touchdown drives and came down to the final minute.

recap.recap: Texas A&M dominated South Carolina from start to finish to retain the belt with a commanding 44-14 victory. The Aggies struck quickly when Ainias Smith returned a punt 95 yards for a touchdown in the first quarter, then added two more scores from quarterback Zach Calzada to Jalen Wydermyer before halftime. South Carolina's offense was repeatedly stymied, coughing up three turnovers including a crucial fumble recovery by Aaron Hansford in the red zone in the second quarter that ended any momentum the Gamecocks might have built. Texas A&M's defense and special teams kept the pressure on throughout, with kicker Seth Small contributing three field goals as the Aggies controlled time of possession 35:30 to 24:30 and piled up 477 total yards.

key_moments: Seth Small's four field goals (21, 29, 47, 37 yards) providing all of Texas A&M's scoring and establishing early field position
Jayden Peevy's forced fumble on Bo Nix in Q4 leading to a recovered fumble and subsequent two-point conversion extending Texas A&M's lead to 20-3
Bo Nix's interception to Jaylon Jones with 2:43 left in Q4 sealing the game for Texas A&M
Auburn's offensive struggles reflected in only two field goals despite 226 total yards and inability to convert opportunities into touchdowns
recap.recap: Texas A&M's defense dominated Auburn in Kyle Field, forcing two crucial turnovers to secure a 20-3 victory and retain the belt. The Aggies' offense moved the ball methodically, with Seth Small providing a steady kicking game that resulted in four successful field goals throughout the contest. Auburn managed only two field goals despite decent yardage totals, as their offense sputtered when it mattered most, particularly a costly Bo Nix interception to Jaylon Jones with 2:43 remaining in the fourth quarter. A pivotal moment came when Jayden Peevy forced another Nix fumble in the fourth quarter, with Texas A&M recovering and converting it to a two-point play to extend their lead to 20-3. The Aggies' ability to control time of possession and limit Auburn's third-down efficiency proved decisive in keeping their lineal claim alive.

key_moments: Matt Corral's 2-yard touchdown pass to Dontario Drummond in Q1 gave Ole Miss an early 10-3 lead
Snoop Conner's 13-yard touchdown run in Q4 pushed Ole Miss back ahead 26-16
AJ Finley's 52-yard pick-six in Q4 provided the decisive score in Ole Miss's 29-19 belt-clinching victory
recap.recap: Ole Miss dominated the first half behind Matt Corral and a powerful ground game, scoring a touchdown pass to Dontario Drummond in the first quarter and adding a field goal to take a 13-0 lead into halftime. Texas A&M mounted a second-half comeback, with Devon Achane punching in a touchdown run in the third quarter and Seth Small adding field goals to make it competitive. The game turned in the fourth quarter when Ole Miss's Snoop Conner scored on a 13-yard run to extend the lead, but Texas A&M's Calzada threw two crucial interceptions—including a 52-yard pick-six to AJ Finley—that sealed the Rebels' 29-19 victory and their claim to the belt.

key_moments: Matt Corral's early passing drives, including touchdown passes to Ealy (Q1) and Drummond (Q2), established Ole Miss's early control and set the tone for the defense
Ole Miss's fourth-quarter touchdown by Henry Parrish Jr. extending the lead to 31-10 and essentially clinching the belt defense
Ethan Barr's interception of Mike Wright late in the fourth quarter at the goal line, preventing Vanderbilt from scoring late and ending any comeback hopes
recap.recap: Ole Miss dominated the first half against Vanderbilt, with Matt Corral orchestrating an efficient passing attack that produced touchdowns to Jerrion Ealy and Dontario Drummond to build a 17-3 halftime lead. Vanderbilt kept pace with field goals from Joseph Bulovas but struggled to consistently move the ball, converting just one third down in the first half. Ole Miss extended their advantage in the fourth quarter with Henry Parrish Jr. punching in a touchdown to reach 31 points, while Vanderbilt's late touchdown to Rocko Griffin proved too little too late. The Rebels' defense stifled Vanderbilt's third-down conversion rate throughout the game despite the Commodores controlling time of possession with their ground game.

key_moments: Snoop Conner's two one-yard touchdown runs in Q2 and Q3 gave Ole Miss an early offensive advantage
Jett Johnson's 48-yard interception return in Q4 set up Mississippi State's touchdown, keeping the Bulldogs alive
Matt Corral's 4-yard rushing touchdown in Q4 extended Ole Miss's lead to provide cushion against the comeback
Jo'quavious Marks' 11-yard touchdown with two-point conversion late in Q4 made it close but came too late
recap.recap: Ole Miss held off a late Mississippi State surge to retain the belt with a 31-21 victory in Starkville. The Rebels' offense dominated time of possession and third-down conversions, with Matt Corral orchestrating multiple scoring drives while Snoop Conner punched in two first-quarter touchdowns to build an early advantage. Mississippi State's Will Rogers kept his team competitive through the air, but costly missed field goals by Nolan McCord in the second quarter and a late interception to Jett Johnson prevented the Bulldogs from mounting a complete comeback despite Jo'quavious Marks' late touchdown run with a two-point conversion making it close.

key_moments: Al Walcott 96-yard interception return for touchdown in Q2 -- gave Baylor early control after Ole Miss had moved into scoring position
Monaray Baldwin 48-yard touchdown run in Q4 -- extended Baylor's lead to double digits when Ole Miss was trying to mount a comeback
Four interceptions by Baylor defense -- systematic dismantling of Ole Miss's passing game proved to be the difference in securing the belt
recap.recap: Baylor's defense dominated Ole Miss in this Cotton Bowl matchup, forcing four interceptions to secure the College Football Belt with a 21-7 victory. Ole Miss struck first with an early field goal attempt that missed, but the Bears' defense took over when Al Walcott returned an interception 96 yards for a touchdown in the second quarter to give Baylor an early lead. Though Ole Miss answered with a Braylon Sanders touchdown reception in the third quarter to cut it to 7-7, Baylor's ground game and defensive pressure proved too much, with Monaray Baldwin scoring on a 48-yard run and Gerry Bohanon finding Tyquan Thornton for a touchdown in the fourth quarter to put the game away. Ole Miss's offense, led by Luke Altmyer, struggled with accuracy and decision-making throughout, coughing up the ball repeatedly and missing two field goal attempts.

key_moments: Mar'Keise Irving's 36-yard run to the BYU 2-yard line in Q1 set up Oregon's first touchdown and established the Ducks' rushing dominance
Troy Franklin's 50-yard reception in Q2 and his 24-yard gain in Q3 gave Oregon explosive plays that BYU's defense couldn't contain
Terrance Ferguson's two touchdown receptions (15 yards in Q2, 9 yards in Q3) showcased Oregon's ability to consistently finish drives in the red zone
BYU's missed 38-yard field goal attempt in Q2 and failed two-point conversion in Q4 represented critical scoring opportunities that slipped away
recap.recap: Oregon dominated the Lineal Championship matchup against BYU, establishing control early with Bo Nix orchestrating an efficient offensive attack. The Ducks struck first with a 2-yard Nix run in the first quarter, then added a field goal before BYU answered with Isaac Rex's 28-yard touchdown reception in the second quarter. Oregon's offense was relentless, with Nix connecting on deep shots to Troy Franklin (50 yards) and finding Terrance Ferguson twice for scores, while the ground game contributed key plays like Mar'Keise Irving's 36-yard run to set up a touchdown. BYU's passing attack, led by Jaren Hall, kept pace statistically but couldn't overcome Oregon's superior execution in the trenches and red zone efficiency, as the Ducks scored touchdowns on five of their first six drives before cruising to the 41-20 victory and claiming the belt.

key_moments: Francisco Mauigoa's 95-yard interception return for a touchdown in Q2, which gave Oregon a 21-13 lead and proved to be the pivotal defensive play
Troy Franklin's 50-yard touchdown reception in the final minute, capped by Bo Nix's two-point conversion run, which sealed Oregon's belt defense
Cameron Ward's interception in Q4 (14:56), which halted Washington State's momentum when the game was still within reach
De'Zhaun Stribling's 15-yard touchdown reception in Q3, which kept Washington State's comeback bid alive
recap.recap: Oregon's defense delivered the decisive blow in this high-scoring Pac-12 battle, as Francisco Mauigoa's 95-yard interception return for a touchdown in the second quarter proved to be the difference-maker in the 44-41 result. Washington State's Cameron Ward kept the Cougars competitive throughout, leading multiple scoring drives and connecting with receivers like De'Zhaun Stribling for touchdowns, but Oregon's Bo Nix orchestrated a more balanced offensive attack that accumulated 624 total yards. The game remained tight into the fourth quarter with both teams trading touchdowns, but Oregon's final drive capped by Troy Franklin's 50-yard touchdown reception with Bo Nix's two-point conversion sealed the belt defense for the Ducks. Despite Washington State's valiant effort and superior passing yards, the turnover margin and Mauigoa's defensive touchdown proved decisive in a game that showcased two potent offenses.

key_moments: Bo Nix's 49-yard TD pass to Chase Cota (Q1) -- established Oregon's early dominance
Oregon's ground game and three second-quarter TDs -- built a commanding lead that Stanford couldn't overcome
Bo Nix's 80-yard touchdown run (Q3) -- sealed the game with an explosive offensive play
Stanford's late-game scoring with Higgins and Patu TDs -- kept the game respectable but couldn't threaten Oregon's lead
recap.recap: Oregon dominated this Pac-12 matchup from start to finish, establishing control early with Camden Lewis's field goal and Bo Nix's 49-yard touchdown pass to Chase Cota in the first quarter. The Ducks' ground game proved devastating throughout, with Bucky Irving and the Oregon rushing attack accumulating 351 yards and controlling the line of scrimmage. Stanford kept things competitive in the second half, with Tanner McKee connecting on two touchdown passes to Elijah Higgins and Casey Filkins to Higgins, but Oregon's explosive plays—including an 80-yard Nix touchdown run in the third quarter—proved too much to overcome. Despite Stanford's late scoring surge with Ari Patu's receiving touchdown in the fourth quarter, Oregon's balanced attack and early cushion were insurmountable, allowing the Ducks to retain the belt with the 45-27 victory.

key_moments: Noah Whittington's 55-yard touchdown run in Q1 gave Oregon an early lead they would never relinquish
Jayden de Laura's interception in Q3 at Oregon's 43-yard line stopped Arizona's momentum and led to another Ducks score
Bo Nix's multiple rushing and passing touchdowns in Q2 put the game out of reach before halftime
Oregon's ground attack accumulating 306 rushing yards, exemplified by James, Irving, and Whittington scores, overwhelmed Arizona's defense
recap.recap: Oregon dominated Arizona from start to finish, with the Ducks' ground game proving too powerful for the Wildcats' defense. After Arizona's Tyler Loop opened the scoring with a field goal in the first quarter, Oregon responded with a pair of quick touchdowns, including a spectacular 55-yard run by Noah Whittington, and never looked back. Bo Nix orchestrated a devastating second-quarter offensive display, throwing and running for multiple scores while Arizona managed only a 52-yard touchdown run by DJ Williams to stay within striking distance before halftime. Oregon put the game away in the third quarter with four more touchdowns, including another Nix rushing score and a 23-yard touchdown run by Bucky Irving, while Arizona's offense continued to struggle despite Jayden de Laura's occasional big plays to receivers like Dorian Singer.

key_moments: Bo Nix's two-touchdown pass drive late in Q2 to Troy Franklin (49 yards, then 2 yards) that pushed Oregon's lead to double digits before halftime
Jordan James's 2-yard rushing touchdown in Q2 that capped Oregon's second-quarter onslaught and put the game out of reach
UCLA's early offensive success with Thompson-Robinson's 36-yard touchdown pass to Keegan Jones that kept the Bruins competitive initially
Dorian Thompson-Robinson's interception in Q4 that resulted in a touchback, eliminating a late UCLA scoring opportunity when they were trying to mount a comeback
recap.recap: Oregon's defense and special teams set the tone early, with Camden Lewis connecting on a 44-yard field goal in the first quarter before UCLA answered with Nicholas Barr-Mira's 47-yarder. The Ducks' offense exploded in the second quarter, with Bo Nix leading a surgical assault that featured touchdown passes to Terrance Ferguson and Troy Franklin (twice), bookended by a Jordan James rushing touchdown to build a commanding halftime lead. UCLA kept pace early with Dorian Thompson-Robinson's 36-yard touchdown pass to Keegan Jones, but Oregon's depth proved too much, as Nix added another scoring pass to Cam McCormick in the third quarter and Bucky Irving in the fourth. A late UCLA touchdown to Jake Bobo made the final score respectable, but Oregon's dominance in time of possession (33:27 to 26:33) and zero turnovers sealed the belt defense.

key_moments: Trikweze Bridges' interception return of a Jack Plummer pass with 2:29 left in Q2, leading to Oregon's third consecutive touchdown drive
Bo Nix's touchdown run with 4:14 in Q2 followed immediately by a 29-yard completion to Irving, exemplifying Oregon's offensive dominance
Noah Whittington's 29-yard touchdown reception with 12:45 in Q3, extending Oregon's lead to insurmountable levels
Jack Plummer's four interceptions throughout the game, with three coming in crucial moments during Oregon's second-quarter scoring spree
recap.recap: Oregon's defense forced four interceptions against California quarterback Jack Plummer, setting up multiple scoring opportunities in a dominant 42-24 victory that kept the belt in Eugene. The Ducks' passing game, led by Bo Nix and receivers like Kris Hutson and Bucky Irving, dissected Cal's defense throughout the game, with Nix accounting for five touchdowns on the day. California mounted an early challenge, with Plummer connecting with Jeremiah Hunter for a 57-yard gain and J. Michael Sturdivant for a touchdown to briefly keep pace, but Oregon's relentless scoring drives—including three consecutive touchdown drives spanning the end of the second quarter—proved too much to overcome. The turning point came in the second quarter when Oregon scored three touchdowns in four minutes of game time, with Nix's back-to-back rushing touchdowns and a 12-yard touchdown pass to Irving extending the lead to insurmountable levels.

key_moments: Bo Nix's early touchdown passes to Conerly Jr. and the creative Bucky Irving-to-Nix TD in Q1 established Oregon's offensive dominance immediately
Shrout's two third-quarter interceptions to Christian Gonzalez set up easy Oregon touchdowns and effectively ended any Colorado comeback hopes
Moliki Matavao's 16-yard touchdown reception late in the first half extended Oregon's lead to 28-7 and demonstrated their suffocating offensive efficiency
recap.recap: Oregon dominated Colorado from start to finish, establishing control early with back-to-back touchdown passes from Bo Nix to Josh Conerly Jr. and an unconventional score on a pass from Bucky Irving to Nix in the first quarter. The Ducks continued their aerial assault throughout the first half, with Nix finding multiple receivers in the end zone before halftime, while Colorado managed only a single 81-yard touchdown connection between J.T. Shrout and Jordyn Tyson to stay within shouting distance. The third quarter proved decisive as Oregon's defense forced two interceptions from Shrout, with Christian Gonzalez returning one 36 yards and another 41 yards, leading directly to short-field touchdowns that put the game completely out of reach. Oregon's relentless offensive execution and Colorado's three turnovers made this a one-sided affair in Boulder, and the Ducks' belt defense was never seriously threatened.

recap.recap: In a high-scoring battle at Autzen Stadium, Washington claimed the College Football Belt with a 37-34 victory over Oregon in a back-and-forth affair that saw both offenses consistently find the end zone. The Ducks struck first with Wayne Taulapapa's 13-yard touchdown run in the opening minutes, but Oregon answered with Bo Nix's 10-yard rushing touchdown in the second quarter to take the lead. The third quarter became a shootout, with both teams trading touchdowns as Michael Penix Jr. led Washington's aerial assault—including a massive 76-yard scoring strike to Ja'Lynn Polk—while Nix countered with a 46-yard touchdown pass to Dont'e Thornton and a 67-yard bomb to Troy Franklin. In the decisive fourth quarter, Washington's Penix connected with Taj Davis for a 62-yard touchdown, and Peyton Henry's final 43-yard field goal with 51 seconds remaining proved to be the difference-maker in securing the belt for the Huskies.

Michael Penix Jr. to Jalen McMillan 27-yard TD pass extended Washington's lead early and showcased the passing attack
Wayne Taulapapa's 57-yard run in Q3 broke open the game and led to another Washington touchdown
Colorado's lone touchdown—a 69-yard pass to Montana Lemonious-Craig—came too late to matter in the lopsided affair
recap.recap: Washington dominated Colorado from start to finish, with the Huskies' defense and special teams setting the tone early. Wayne Taulapapa scored on Washington's opening drive with an 8-yard TD run, and the momentum never shifted as Michael Penix Jr. connected with Jalen McMillan for a 27-yard touchdown just minutes later. Colorado managed only a safety late in the second quarter when a run play went for 31 yards in the wrong direction, but Washington answered immediately with Cameron Davis scoring on a 4-yard run before halftime. The third quarter saw Washington's ground game take over, with Taulapapa breaking off a 57-yard run to set up another Davis touchdown, followed by Richard Newton punching in a 2-yard score, and though Colorado found the end zone with a 69-yard touchdown pass to Montana Lemonious-Craig late in the quarter, it was too little too late. Dylan Morris entered in the fourth quarter and led Washington to another touchdown, putting the final nail in the coffin in a complete defensive and offensive performance that kept the belt firmly in Seattle.

key_moments: Michael Penix Jr.'s 75-yard touchdown pass to Jalen McMillan in Q3 -- extended Washington's lead to a commanding margin
Michael Penix Jr.'s two rushing touchdowns in Q2 (30 yards and 4 yards) -- exemplified the Huskies' balanced attack and scoring efficiency
Penix's interception in Q3 resulting in a touchback -- gave Washington State good field position but the Huskies' defense held firm
Rome Odunze's two 47+ yard touchdown receptions in Q2 -- established Washington's dominant passing game that Washington State's secondary couldn't contain
recap.recap: Washington dominated the Alamo Bowl matchup against Washington State with a balanced offensive attack, racking up 703 total yards while holding the Cougars to 433. Michael Penix Jr. was the star of the show, engineering multiple scoring drives throughout the game, including a spectacular 75-yard touchdown pass to Jalen McMillan in the third quarter that gave the Huskies decisive momentum. Despite Cameron Ward's solid performance for Washington State and a two-point conversion on a Nakia Watson touchdown run in the third quarter, the hosts couldn't keep pace with Penix's efficiency and Washington's superior third-down conversion rate of 11-13. Washington's defense forced two critical turnovers, including an interception in the third quarter that resulted in a touchback, and the Huskies' offense answered nearly every Washington State score with drives of their own, particularly in the second quarter when they scored four touchdowns to pull away decisively.

key_moments: Chase Roberts 20-yard TD reception with 2 seconds left in Q2 to give BYU a 10-7 halftime lead
Jaren Hall's 22-yard TD pass to Chase Roberts in Q3 to extend BYU's lead after Baylor tied it
Lopini Katoa's 3-yard TD run in the final moments to secure BYU's 26-20 victory and the belt
recap.recap: BYU claimed the College Football Belt with a 26-20 victory over Baylor in Provo, overcoming a Bears team that controlled the line of scrimmage and time of possession. The Cougars struck first with a Jake Oldroyd field goal in the first quarter, then took a 10-7 halftime lead when Jaren Hall connected with Chase Roberts for a 20-yard touchdown with just two seconds left in the half. Baylor answered with a Qualan Jones touchdown run in the third quarter to tie it, but BYU responded with an Oldroyd field goal and a spectacular 22-yard touchdown pass from Hall to Roberts (technically a reverse) to seize control. In a back-and-forth fourth quarter, Blake Shapen led the Bears to another score to make it 23-20, setting up a dramatic finish where BYU's Lopini Katoa punched in a 3-yard touchdown run to secure the belt, though the two-point conversion failed.

Gavin Holmes' 72-yard punt return for a touchdown in Q1 was UAlbany's best scoring opportunity, but Baylor answered before halftime
Richard Reese's rushing touchdown in Q4 exemplified Baylor's complete control of the game in the second half
The early turnover by UAlbany (Jackson Parker fumble in Q1) set the stage for Baylor's efficient offensive performance with zero turnovers
recap.recap: Baylor dominated UAlbany from start to finish, establishing control early with a Blake Shapen touchdown pass to Monaray Baldwin just under 11 minutes into the first quarter. The game featured several explosive plays, including a remarkable 72-yard punt return for a touchdown by Gavin Holmes that briefly gave UAlbany hope at 14-10, but Baylor answered immediately with another score before halftime. The Bears' ground game took over in the second half, with Richard Reese and Monaray Baldwin combining for multiple rushing touchdowns to put the game completely out of reach. UAlbany's only points came from a pair of passing touchdowns by Reese Poffenbarger to Julian Hicks and a field goal, but they could never generate sustained offensive momentum against Baylor's defense.

key_moments: Jerrin Thompson's first-quarter interception of Michael Penix Jr., which gave Washington prime field position and led to the opening field goal
Wayne Taulapapa's 42-yard rushing touchdown in Q1 that gave Washington a 10-3 lead and set the tone for the game
Michael Penix Jr.'s touchdown pass to Jalen McMillan in the fourth quarter that pushed Washington's lead to 27-13, effectively sealing the belt defense
recap.recap: Washington's defense forced an early interception to Quinn Ewers, setting up Peyton Henry's 46-yard field goal for the game's first score. The Huskies struck quickly in the first quarter when Wayne Taulapapa broke through for a 42-yard touchdown run to take a commanding 10-3 lead. Texas answered with a touchdown pass from Ewers to Jonathon Brooks covering 34 yards in the third quarter, but Washington maintained control with touchdown passes from Michael Penix Jr. to Taj Davis and Jalen McMillan in the fourth quarter. Despite Texas mounting a late comeback with a Brooks rushing touchdown and a field goal, the Huskies' 27-20 victory was sealed by superior third-down efficiency (11-20 vs 6-15) and time of possession dominance (35:46 to 24:14), allowing them to hold onto the belt.

key_moments: Penix's 50-yard completion to Rome Odunze in Q2 set up Washington's third touchdown and exemplified the Huskies' dominant passing efficiency throughout the game

Noah Kim's interception in Q1 with 2:21 remaining gave Washington prime field position and led directly to another Penix touchdown pass, effectively ending any momentum Michigan State might have built
Washington's four passing touchdowns in the first half (to Polk, Westover twice, and another to Westover) established a commanding lead that Michigan State never threatened to overcome
Grady Gross's two field goals in Q3 extended Washington's lead to 41 points and eliminated any remaining drama from the contest
recap.recap: Washington's high-powered passing attack dominated Michigan State from start to finish, with Michael Penix Jr. orchestrating a clinic in efficient offensive football to keep the belt firmly around the Huskies' waist. The game was essentially decided in the first half, as Washington scored five touchdowns in the opening two quarters, including four passing TDs to three different receivers and a rushing score, while Michigan State managed only a single drive of note late in the second quarter. Penix connected repeatedly with Rome Odunze, Ja'Lynn Polk, and Jack Westover throughout the contest, accumulating 536 passing yards on an efficient day that saw Washington control the game with a dominant 35:32 time-of-possession advantage. Michigan State's Noah Kim was intercepted early and the Spartans' 261 total yards of offense proved completely insufficient to challenge a Washington team that generated 713 yards and methodically bled the clock, with the Huskies adding two field goals in the second half to put the game completely out of reach.

key_moments: Michael Penix Jr. to Jalen McMillan 7-yard TD pass (Q2 14:09) — Washington's first score broke the ice after Boise State's opening drive touchdown
Penix to Ja'Lynn Polk 44-yard TD pass (Q2 5:06) — Part of Washington's devastating four-score second-quarter explosion that put the game out of reach
Taylen Green interception to Kamren Fabiculanan (Q2 2:10) — Turnover halted Boise State momentum and led directly to Washington's fourth touchdown drive
Ashton Jeanty 50-yard TD reception from Green (Q3 12:49) — Boise State's only second-half touchdown, but too little too late as Washington had already built a commanding lead
recap.recap: Washington's defense and offense overwhelmed Boise State from start to finish in a dominant 56-19 belt-defense victory. After Boise State struck first with a 7-yard Ashton Jeanty touchdown run, the Huskies erupted behind Michael Penix Jr., who engineered a devastating passing attack that produced four touchdowns in the second quarter alone, including scoring strikes to Jalen McMillan (twice), Ja'Lynn Polk, and Jack Westover. Boise State managed a pair of field goals and a second-half touchdown pass from Taylen Green to Jeanty, but Washington's balanced assault—490 passing yards and relentless efficiency on third down—proved impossible to contain. The Huskies added two more touchdowns in the fourth quarter to cruise to an easy conference road victory and maintain their grip on the lineal championship.

key_moments: Penix to Odunze for 2-yard TD and 50-yard penalty-aided opening drive set the tone for Washington's offensive dominance
Polk's 27-yard rushing touchdown in Q1 extended the lead and established Washington's balanced attack
McMillan's 9-yard TD reception with two-point conversion in Q2 pushed the lead to insurmountable levels before halftime
Germie Bernard's 7-yard TD reception in Q3 and Odunze's rushing TD late in Q3 put the game completely out of reach
recap.recap: Washington dominated from the opening drive, with Michael Penix Jr. orchestrating an efficient offense that struck quickly and often. After an early 50-yard penalty-aided drive resulted in a Rome Odunze touchdown, the Huskies extended their lead with a Ja'Lynn Polk rushing touchdown in the first quarter, and continued their assault with a Jalen McMillan touchdown reception and two-point conversion in the second quarter. Tulsa managed only a Chase Meyer field goal in the first half and never seriously threatened, as Washington's defense kept the visitors bottled up with just 318 total yards while Penix completed pass after pass to receivers like Odunze and Bernard. The Huskies sealed the dominant performance with scores in the third quarter before substitutes mopped up late, with an early interception and a McMillan fumble the only blemishes on an otherwise flawless belt-defending effort.

Rome Odunze's 83-yard punt return touchdown that kept California in the game early
Michael Penix Jr.'s four touchdown passes to Rome Odunze, demonstrating Washington's offensive dominance and the inability of California's defense to stop the connection
Multiple Ben Finley interceptions throughout the game that resulted in turnovers at critical moments
recap.recap: Washington's defense set the tone early with an interception return touchdown by Edefuan Ulofoshio just 12:37 into the game, but California answered back immediately with Rome Odunze's 83-yard punt return for a touchdown. The game became a shootout between Michael Penix Jr. and Ben Finley, with Washington's offense eventually proving too much to handle. Penix Jr. found Rome Odunze repeatedly throughout the game, including four touchdown passes to him, while also connecting with Ja'Lynn Polk for multiple scores. Washington pulled away in the second half after building a commanding lead, with Odunze's third touchdown pass putting the Huskies firmly in control by the third quarter.

key_moments: Germie Bernard's 3-yard TD run in Q1 established early Washington momentum and helped build a first-half lead
Josh Cuevas' 57-yard reception in Q3 kept Washington's offense moving and prevented Arizona from fully capitalizing on their comeback
Tetairoa McMillan's two TD receptions (Q3 and Q4) brought Arizona within reach but came too late to overcome the early deficit
Will Nixon's 5-yard TD run in Q2 gave Washington critical separation that ultimately made the difference in a close contest
recap.recap: Washington's defense and balanced offensive attack proved too much for Arizona in this Pac-12 battle, as the Huskies held onto the College Football Belt with a 31-24 road victory. Washington jumped out to an early lead with two rushing touchdowns in the first quarter from Dillon Johnson and Germie Bernard, then added another TD run from Will Nixon in the second quarter to build a commanding advantage. Arizona mounted a second-half comeback led by Noah Fifita's passing, with Tetairoa McMillan catching two touchdown passes to pull within striking distance, but Washington's offense kept pace with a 57-yard pass to Josh Cuevas and additional field goals to seal the win. The Huskies' ability to establish the run game early and Michael Penix Jr.'s efficient passing kept Arizona's defense off-balance throughout the contest.

key_moments: Penix's early touchdown passes to Giles Jackson and Ja'Lynn Polk in the first quarter gave Washington an early 14-6 lead and set the tone for a strong offensive performance

Penix's go-ahead 18-yard touchdown pass to Rome Odunze with 1:38 left proved to be the game-winner when Oregon's final field goal attempt missed

Washington's turnover margin advantage (1 turnover vs Oregon's 0) was offset by Oregon's superior third-down conversion rate (10-16 vs 5-11), but Washington's late-game execution sealed the belt retention
recap.recap: Washington's high-powered passing attack proved too much for Oregon to overcome in this back-and-forth Pac-12 battle, as the Huskies held onto the belt with a 36-33 victory in Eugene. Michael Penix Jr. was the star of the show, orchestrating several crucial scoring drives and connecting with his receivers repeatedly, including a go-ahead touchdown pass to Rome Odunze for 18 yards with just 1:38 remaining in the game. Oregon kept pace throughout, with Bo Nix leading impressive drives and Troy Franklin making several big plays, but the Ducks couldn't capitalize in the final moments when Camden Lewis's 43-yard field goal attempt missed as time expired. The turning point came late in the fourth quarter when Washington's defense forced Oregon into a critical situation, and Penix's last-minute precision passing sealed the belt-holding victory.

key_moments: Grady Gross's three field goals (24, 47, and 24 yards) providing the offensive firepower Washington needed in a low-scoring affair
Michael Penix Jr.'s two first-half interceptions and fumble recovery by ASU that could have derailed Washington but the defense held firm
Cameron Skattebo's 1-yard touchdown run in Q2 giving Arizona State a 7-3 lead but failing to extend it further
Mishael Powell's 89-yard interception return for a touchdown in Q4 that failed on the two-point conversion, representing Arizona State's last real chance to win
recap.recap: Washington's defense proved stifling in this defensive struggle, with the Huskies holding the belt despite a lopsided yardage advantage for Arizona State. The Sun Devils dominated time of possession 37:29 to 22:31 and rushed for 145 yards, but Washington's defense forced four turnovers and limited ASU to just 15 points. Michael Penix Jr. was intercepted twice early in the game, but Washington's kicker Grady Gross made three field goals to secure the 15-7 victory. Arizona State's only touchdown came on a Cameron Skattebo 1-yard run in the second quarter, while ASU's late interception return for a touchdown by Mishael Powell (89 yards in the fourth quarter) and subsequent two-point conversion failure sealed their fate with just minutes remaining.

key_moments: Ja'Lynn Polk's 92-yard touchdown reception late in Q2 gave Washington momentum and a lead they wouldn't relinquish
Michael Penix Jr.'s three touchdown passes to Rome Odunze provided consistent scoring threats throughout the game
Stanford's failed two-point conversion in Q3 after Elic Ayomanor's touchdown catch kept Washington's lead intact

recap.recap: Washington's defense held firm in the second half to preserve the belt with a 33-42 victory at Stanford. Notre Dame's balanced attack and turnover discipline, committing zero turnovers compared to Wisconsin's two, proved decisive in the 41-13 victory that allowed the Irish to retain the belt.
